backlog.spec: Change how the pool is updated in solve; the pool size stays 5. Define the distance between two packings as the L2 norm of the difference of their descending-sorted radius vectors. When a new packing arrives and the pool is full: find the pool member closest to it; if that distance is below 0.02, the new packing replaces that member only if its radius sum is larger (otherwise it is dropped); if no member is that close, it replaces the worst member if its radius sum is larger than the worst. This keeps the pool from filling with copies of one basin, so crossover mixes really different packings. The best-so-far tracking and everything else stay the same.
backlog.title: Crowding replacement in the pool

backlog.spec: Currently _cross always cuts vertically at x=t. Choose the cut axis at random per crossover: with probability 0.5 use x as now, otherwise use y (keep circles with centre y below t from parent a and y at or above t from parent b). Draw t uniformly from [0.3, 0.7] as before. Filling of missing circles and trimming of surplus circles stay unchanged.
backlog.title: Random cut axis in crossover

backlog.spec: Change the pool update from keep-top-5 to deterministic crowding with a pool of 8. A new packing whose sum is better than the worst pool member replaces the pool member with the closest sorted radius vector (L2), but only if the new packing is better than that member. Otherwise it replaces the worst member, but only when the closest L2 distance exceeds 1e-3. This keeps several distinct basins alive for crossover. The best is tracked separately as now.
backlog.title: Pool replacement by nearest neighbour (crowding)

backlog.spec: Replace half of the fresh random x0 with a greedy start. Place the first centre uniformly at random. For each next circle, sample 400 random candidate points and pick the one that maximises min(distance to the nearest placed centre minus that centre's provisional radius, distance to the nearest wall). Set its provisional radius to 0.9 times that clearance, capped at 0.15. Use the centres and provisional radii (floored at 0.01) as x0 for _solve_once. Use the solve rng only.
backlog.title: Greedy largest-hole sequential insertion starts

backlog.spec: Split the search time (TIME_FRACTION * time_limit) into four equal phases. In phases 1 to 3 run the existing loop (fresh starts, 70% crossover once the pool has 2, pool of 5) with a separate, initially empty pool per phase, all drawing from the same seeded rng. In phase 4 form a merged pool from the best 2 packings of each island (6 members, keep pool size 6) and run the same loop with crossover probability 0.9. Return the best packing seen in any phase. This gives three independent populations per seed and then recombines their best, to reduce the seed-to-seed spread.
backlog.title: Three islands, then a merged final phase

backlog.spec: Split the restart loop into 3 equal time slices of TIME_FRACTION*time_limit/3. Each slice has its own empty pool of 5, so crossover only mixes packings found in that slice. Keep a global best across slices and return it. The aim is to avoid early pool collapse onto one basin. No other changes.
backlog.title: Three independent sub-run portfolio

backlog.spec: Replace uniform random fresh starts by a greedy construction. Sample 600 candidate points uniformly in the unit square once per start. Draw a radius cap for this start uniformly in [0.08, 0.13]. Then n times: for every candidate compute its clearance = min(distance to the 4 walls, distance to each placed centre minus that circle's radius); among the 10 candidates with the largest clearance pick one at random using the seeded rng; place a circle there with radius min(cap, clearance) * 0.9. If the clearance is not positive, place radius 0.005 at a random point. Use these centres and radii as x0 for SLSQP. Crossover starts, the pool, the repair step and the time loop stay the same.
backlog.title: Greedy max-clearance constructive starts

backlog.spec: Replace uniform random fresh centres in _solve_once with scrambled Sobol points. Use scipy.stats.qmc.Sobol(d=2, scramble=True, seed=int(rng.integers(2**31))).random(32)[:n], mapped affinely into [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2 and then given Gaussian jitter of sd 0.01. Radii stay at INIT_RADIUS. The more even spread should start SLSQP with fewer badly overlapping circles. The crossover and pool are unchanged.
backlog.title: Scrambled Sobol fresh centres

backlog.spec: Add a restart type with probability 0.3. Take a random pool member, pick two circles with different radii that are neighbours (centre distance below 1.2 times the sum of their radii), and swap their centres. Keep the radii as they are, shrink all radii by 10 percent and run SLSQP. This tests exchanges of big and small circles without large perturbation. Use it alongside the slot 11 relaxation.
backlog.title: Swap-radius moves between neighbouring circles

backlog.spec: Replace the sorted-radius diversity test with a centre-based test. Before adding a new packing to the pool, compute for each existing member the mean over circles of the distance from each centre to its nearest centre in the other packing. If the minimum of this value over the pool is below 0.02, the new packing is a near duplicate: keep only the one with the larger radius sum. Otherwise insert it and keep the top 8 by radius sum. Everything else (crossover, perturbation, time loop) stays as in the incumbent.
backlog.title: Centre-based diversity filter for the pool

backlog.spec: Adopt slot 11 as base: for fresh random starts, relax centres with L-BFGS-B on a smooth overlap/wall penalty energy with target radii about 0.09 before SLSQP. Also use a pool of 12 with a diversity filter that skips packings whose sorted radius vector is within 1e-3 L2 of a pool member. Crossover and jitter restarts draw from this pool. Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Penalty relaxation on fresh starts plus pool of 12

backlog.spec: After the restart loop has used the first 60% of the time budget, run a simulated-annealing phase on the best packing. Each move picks one random circle, moves its centre by a Gaussian step with sd 0.05 (clipped into the box), and recomputes all radii with the greedy clearance rule (each radius is the largest value satisfying walls and neighbours, given the other radii held fixed in a sweep). Accept the move with the Metropolis rule at temperature decreasing linearly from 0.002 to 0. Keep the best state seen. Run this until the time budget is used. The pool and SLSQP restarts still run for the first part of the time.
backlog.title: Single-circle Metropolis moves on the best packing

backlog.spec: Fresh starts: 50 percent a noisy staggered lattice (row counts random in 5 to 7, noise sd 0.02), 50 percent uniform random. All are relaxed by penalty L-BFGS-B. Use pool 12 with the 1e-3 sorted-radius filter and 70 percent crossover from the pool. This combines slots 32 and 18 for a replicated run.
backlog.title: Noisy lattice starts with penalty relaxation, pool 12

backlog.spec: For fresh random starts, draw the initial centres from a low-discrepancy set instead of uniform random. Build a 2D Halton point set with bases 2 and 3 of size n, shifted by a random offset drawn from rng (with modulo 1 wrap-around), and map it into [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2. Use these centres and INIT_RADIUS radii as the SLSQP start. Keep the crossover and pool logic unchanged, so only the fresh-start distribution differs.
backlog.title: Scrambled van der Corput centres for fresh starts

backlog.spec: Change _cross so that it cuts along a line in a random direction instead of the x-threshold. Draw an angle theta uniformly in [0, pi) and a unit vector u = (cos theta, sin theta). Project the centres of both parents onto u. Pick k = rng.integers(10, n-9). Take the k circles of parent A with the smallest projections, then fill with the circles of parent B, in increasing projection order, whose projection exceeds the k-th projection of A, until there are n circles. If B runs out, add random circles of radius INIT_RADIUS. The child always has exactly n circles, so no random dropping is needed.
backlog.title: Random-angle median cut crossover

backlog.spec: For fresh starts, solve the SLSQP problem with n+k circles (k=2) instead of n, using random centres and INIT_RADIUS radii. After the solve, sort by radius and delete the k smallest circles, then clip, repair and score the remaining n circles as usual. The extra circles give the optimiser room to rearrange, and the discard step keeps the output at exactly n circles. Keep the pool logic unchanged.
backlog.title: Overcomplete start, drop the smallest circles

backlog.spec: For fresh starts (no crossover), build the initial centres one at a time. Sample 2000 candidate points uniformly in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2 with rng, and place the next centre at the candidate whose distance to the nearest existing centre (and to the walls) is largest. Initial radii are INIT_RADIUS for all circles. Keep the rest of the loop unchanged. The rest of the pipeline (SLSQP, repair, pool) stays as in slot 11.
backlog.title: Greedy largest-empty-circle initialisation

backlog.spec: Pass ftol to the SLSQP call. For fresh random starts use ftol=1e-5 so each run stops early and more restarts fit into the budget. For restarts seeded from the pool (crossover and perturbation), use ftol=1e-10 and the existing MAX_ITER. Keep the existing constraint set and repair. This only changes the stopping rule of the solver, not the formulation.
backlog.title: Loose tolerance for fresh starts, tight tolerance for pool polish

backlog.spec: Replace the crossover restarts (70 percent of the time) with a relocation move. Pick a pool member, pick one circle with probability proportional to 1/radius, and move it to a random location. Set its radius to 0.03, then run SLSQP. Combine with penalty-relaxed fresh starts and a pool of 12 with the 1e-3 diversity filter.
backlog.title: Relocation moves on pool members

backlog.spec: Keep the slot 11 setup. Change SHRINK from 1e-9 to 1e-12, and make _repair run a second pass that verifies exactly in double precision that every pair distance minus the radii sum is at least 1e-11 and every wall gap is at least 1e-11. If a pair violates this, shrink its two radii by the overlap. This recovers about 1e-8 per circle with no validity risk.
backlog.title: Final exact feasibility polish with tighter shrink

memo:
Helped: slot 0, a pool of the 5 best packings with SLSQP restarts from perturbed pool members (-2.9334, the only accepted change). Penalty-energy L-BFGS-B relaxation of fresh starts is the strongest signal: slot 11 gave -2.9396 on both of 2 runs, and slot 32 (noisy lattice or random starts, relaxed) also gave -2.9396/-2.9396. Slot 38 gave -2.9396/-2.9386. Diverse pool of 12 with the 1e-3 filter also helped (slot 18 -2.9386/-2.9349, slot 9 -2.9368), as did relocation (slot 29 -2.9396/-2.9360).
Did not help: schedule/time-fraction tuning (slots 1-6, within noise sd 0.0034), basin-hopping jitter (-2.9323), boundary-circle init (-2.9300), drop-and-resample (-2.9307), smallest-circle reinsertion (-2.9237), LP repair (-2.9297), multi-stage or reduced-constraint SLSQP (as low as -2.9044), analytic gradients (no change).
Next: adopt slot 11 as the base (-2.9396 replicated). Combine it with the pool of 12 and the 1e-3 filter, then add relocation. Avoid schedule tuning, large perturbations and repeating aborted ideas.
